title: KLC – detailed help and functional reference
release_note: Advanced field and operating aid with short tooltips and context-related help references in seven languages.

sections.title: Start-up – complete workflow
sections.body:
1. Use the matching hardware profile: klc_16m for RP2350-Plus with W5500, klc_16m_w for RP2350B-Plus-W with Wi-Fi. Software cannot add missing radio hardware.
2. Complete the setup wizard: language, appearance, credentials, outputs and Wi-Fi if applicable. Setup is complete only after a confirmed save.
3. Under Device → Network, check addresses, DHCP and connectivity. Leave automatic network shutdown set to Off during setup.
4. Under Outputs, start with a short test strip. Set LED chip, RGB/RGBW and color order; test red, green, blue and white where applicable on the physical strip.
5. Adapt power supply groups, strip limits, controller limit, safety factor and current profile to the installation.
6. Save each form. Structural changes require the indicated restart; then check the active state and diagnostics.
7. Configure scenes 1 to 30 and check both preview and physical output. Then configure output sequences and KNX behavior.
8. Use the current KLC interface in ETS. Link command and status objects correctly; test lock, force and permission to switch on.
9. Keep a full backup and a separate scene export. Record version and hardware profile with the files.

sections.title: Hardware, LED data and supply
sections.body:
The RP2350 calculates scenes; the W5500 provides Ethernet. The Wi-Fi profile adds a client and service access point. KNX uses the BAOS module over UART. The board profile defines physical outputs and pins; internal array limits do not imply additional terminals.
Addressable LEDs need a suitable supply, common ground, correct data direction and suitable level conversion. Selecting an LED chip does not set the supply voltage. In particular, a 12 V strip still needs the correct supply.
The software estimates current from color values and the current profile. It does not measure cable temperature or replace fuses and appropriately sized wiring. Check a small test installation before increasing load and pixel count.
Device and Support show firmware profile, board ID and hardware assignment. Match these to the firmware file. The old 4 MB variant is discontinued.

sections.title: Navigation, roles and storage
sections.body:
Tabs lead to Home, Outputs, Scenes, Output sequence, KNX, Device and Help. Network, Update, Events, Security, Backup and Support are linked from the relevant areas.
The former simple/advanced view switch has been removed. Roles determine access to protected actions. The controller checks direct API requests too; seeing a link does not grant permission.
Browser edits are drafts. Save or Apply confirms the corresponding change. After an error, the previous valid state remains authoritative. Discard removes unsaved edits; changing pages may show a warning.
For output structures, saved and active differ: a new pixel count or chain becomes active only after a successful restart. Preview tests are temporary and never saved automatically.
Disabled fields may depend on the effect, color type, chain state, an ongoing operation or permissions. Read the adjacent explanation before changing another setting.

sections.title: Home and direct lighting
sections.body:
The home page shows current state, scene and estimated load for each output. Scene selection follows KNX changes; Off remains recognizable. Scene 0 means Off, and 1 to 30 are scene slots.
Central controls affect multiple independent outputs. A chain follower is controlled through its head. Disabled scenes cannot be started normally.
Direct color and brightness values affect the running state. Lock, force, output sequences and manual tests can affect normal commands. For unexpected light, first check the command origin and active tests.
Load is an estimate. An active limit can dim the output below the scene value. Base and standby current are accounted for separately. Use the home page for operation and Outputs for hardware settings.

sections.title: Network: Ethernet, WLAN and accessibility
sections.body:
Device → Network shows connectivity and automatic shutdown. Edit network opens detailed settings. Ethernet (eth0), Wi-Fi client (wlan0) and service AP (ap0) are displayed separately where supported.
Ethernet uses a cable; the Wi-Fi client joins an existing network; the AP creates a maintenance Wi-Fi network. Each displayed IP belongs to its interface.
When Ethernet and Wi-Fi share a subnet, only one interface actively uses that LAN. The other may retain its IP but does not respond on that address while on standby. The status identifies the active connection. Separate subnets are required to reach both addresses simultaneously.
Priority selects the preferred outgoing route, for example for downloads. Local web access does not prove Internet access: gateway, DNS and a valid clock for HTTPS are also needed.
If all interfaces are off, the web interface is unavailable. KNX light control can continue. A KNX ON command or the service button can restore access.

sections.title: Automatic network shutdown and performance
sections.body:
As administrator, open Device → Network → Automatically turn off network after: Off, 1 minute, 30 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours, 6 hours or 24 hours. Save the shutdown time to retain it. Off disables the timer; it does not issue a network OFF command.
With an active timer, Ethernet starts after every reboot, even if previously switched off through KNX. The timer starts with network initialization. Saving a changed time starts a new window. Page requests and mouse movement do not extend it.
At expiry, Ethernet and Wi-Fi, including the AP, stop. The web page is then unreachable. Removing web and network processing can free loop time for LED animation; no fixed percentage improvement is guaranteed.
To regain access, send KNX DP 20 = 1 for Ethernet, DP 21 = 1 for Wi-Fi, or restart. A KNX ON command restarts the timer even when ON is sent again. Reboot enables Ethernet when the timer is active. Holding the service button for at least 2 but less than 5 seconds additionally resets network settings.
Expiry itself does not save permanent OFF states to flash. Before lengthy maintenance or updates, select Off or a sufficiently long interval. The selected interval survives power loss.

sections.title: Ethernet: DHCP, static address and fallback
sections.body:
DHCP obtains address settings from the router or DHCP server. A DHCP reservation can keep the address stable. Static IP, subnet mask, gateway and DNS must match the network; do not assign an address twice.
Device name is the display name; hostname is the network name. Name resolution depends on your network. Use the displayed IP when troubleshooting. A physical link without an IP address differs from an unplugged cable.
Fallback IP provides a separately configured emergency address for problems with regular addressing. Set its IP, gateway, subnet and DNS independently. The maintenance computer must be able to reach that subnet; an unsuitable fallback address does not fix incorrect configuration.
Save Ethernet stores the values. Address settings take effect on the next Ethernet start, so observe restart messages. The interface switch acts at runtime. The web interface prevents some immediate shutdowns of the last connection; KNX and the timer can still turn all interfaces off.
Troubleshoot in order: cable/link, IP assignment, subnet, gateway/router, DNS. Avoid making several conflicting changes at once.

sections.title: Wi-Fi client, service-AP and failover
sections.body:
Wi-Fi is the common master switch for client and access point. Enable client joins the configured SSID. Client DHCP or static addressing is independent of Ethernet. SSID and password must match exactly.
The service AP creates a maintenance network. An empty AP name is generated automatically. AP IP and other active networks must not create an invalid address collision. Use an AP password of 8 to 63 characters, or deliberately choose an open network. Empty password fields on the normal settings page retain saved passwords.
The wizard tests Wi-Fi before completion. A channel change may briefly interrupt service access. Wait for confirmed connection/save status; the AP may stop after successful handover to the home network.
When Ethernet and Wi-Fi share a subnet, the firmware parks one interface to prevent replies using the wrong route. The other can take over after failure. A parked IP is not reachable even if still displayed.
Wi-Fi commands have no effect without radio hardware. No Wi-Fi on klc_16m is expected. Automatic network shutdown also stops the service AP.

sections.title: Outputs: active, stored and tested
sections.body:
Each physical output has a name, enable setting, LED chip, RGB/RGBW type, color order and pixel count. The board profile determines available outputs. Changing the number used can require a restart; when reducing it, check the confirmation and affected outputs.
Active means the hardware configuration has started successfully. Saved means the controller confirmed storage. Structural changes, including pixel count, profile and chains, remain pending until restart. Successful file writing alone does not prove successful PIO/DMA initialization.
Tests can use current form values before saving. They are temporary, use the fixed test pool and are never saved automatically. Stopping or discarding a test restores active state. On navigation, the browser tries to stop its tests; connection loss is monitored too.
If test state is unknown, wait for confirmation from the device. Button color alone does not prove success. Check values, save separately, restart if required and verify active diagnostics.

sections.title: Pixel boundaries, storage plan and recovery
sections.body:
Up to 800 pixels per output is the normal range. 801 to 1200 is allowed with a warning; more than 1200 is rejected. Total pixel and memory limits also apply: multiple individually valid strips may exceed the combined budget.
0 pixels is allowed only for a temporary test without physical output, not as a saved normal configuration. With one pixel, both edge tests address pixel 0.
Four 32-bit buffer components require 16 bytes per pixel. Add 64 blackout pixels per active output and a fixed test pool. The LED budget is 128 KiB, with a separate 64 KiB system reserve. Total free heap differs from the size of a contiguous allocation.
Pending becomes Last Known Good only after validation, pool allocation, PIO/DMA and all outputs start successfully. Failed activation releases its resources and tries the last successful plan. If that fails too, LEDs remain off in safe recovery mode. Pending remains visible for correction and is not retried endlessly.
Diagnostics separate active, pending and last successful plans, and heap before/after activation. Use those exact distinctions when reporting a problem.

sections.title: Chain direction and string segments
sections.body:
Independent means a separately controlled output. A follower extends its predecessor's logical pixel space; the first output is the chain head. Each output may have at most one direct follower, and cycles are forbidden.
The head controls scenes and KNX behavior. Followers do not have independent scene control; LED chip, color type and color order come from the head. Tests protect the whole chain rather than starting a follower alone.
Reverse within chain changes pixel order only for that physical chain member. Use it for opposite mounting direction; it is different from scene direction. The chain-walk test reveals logical order.
Equal string segments divide a physical strip into repeated parts. 1 means no subdivision. Segment count must divide pixel count; the interface selects a suitable divisor. String segmentation and chains cannot be combined arbitrarily.
LED offset adjusts the logical start/center, limited to half the strip length plus 1. Save structural changes and perform the indicated restart.

sections.title: Colour, edge, zero-pixel and chain tests
sections.body:
1. Open the output or chain head and choose an appropriate small pixel count and profile.
2. Start the red edge test, followed by green, blue and white for RGBW. The first and last LEDs must respond at the expected positions.
3. Wrong color: check RGB order. Shifted image: check RGB/RGBW, pixel count and chain. No light: check supply, common ground, data direction, level conversion and enable state.
4. Clicking the same test with unchanged values stops it; changed inputs can restart it. Check the confirmed device state.
5. The chain walk tests the entire logical pixel space. A 0-pixel test produces no PIO/DMA output and is temporary.
6. Stop the test, save intended values and restart if necessary. Then verify a normal scene and ensure no manual test still overrides it.
The test panel may be locked during an operation to prevent Save, Discard and Test from racing. After errors, status is read from the controller again.

sections.title: Start-up behavior and LED-send clock
sections.body:
After power interruption controls only the state after reboot: Off, fixed RGBW percentages or a fixed scene from 1 to 30. It is separate from the KNX switch-on mode.
The last KNX state has its own small storage mechanism. It does not automatically override an explicit startup setting. Choose Off for a defined dark startup.
LED data sending offers 1× per second, 2× per second or every frame. Changes are always sent immediately. Unchanged frames are repeated to recover from a corrupted frame.
Every frame also transmits unchanged animation frames and can require more output time. The old freely configurable send interval is a compatibility field and does not control these three modes.

sections.title: Power Limitation: Limits and Calculations
sections.body:
The current estimate uses output colors, current per channel and pixel, LED standby current and fixed base current. It is not a physical current measurement.
Strip, power-group and controller limits apply together. The smallest required factor limits output. The safety factor further reduces the usable budget. Output maximum brightness and scene brightness also apply.
0 means no individual limit only for a strip limit. Group and controller limits remain active and require positive values. Strip limit: up to 200000 mA. Active group/controller limits: 1 to 300000 mA. 1000 mA = 1 A.
Base current cannot be dimmed. If it exceeds the budget, dimming alone cannot satisfy the limit. Do not count base and standby current twice.
Individual limiting uses each strip separately. Group-coupled limiting applies the smallest required strip factor to its power group to keep adjacent strips at similar brightness.
After saving, use a representative bright scene to compare estimated current before limiting, load after dimming, dimming factor and the active limiting level. Software does not replace fuses or correctly sized wiring.

sections.title: Measuring current profile – complete sequence
sections.body:
Select the test output and the actual number of measurement LEDs. First switch all LEDs off and measure total current in mA. Then run exactly that number of LEDs at full red, green, blue and white for RGBW, entering each measured total current. RGB white is an additional check with all RGB channels on together.
Current per pixel for each channel is the difference from the all-off measurement divided by the LED count. A color measurement below the all-off measurement is implausible. An incorrect LED count corrupts every calculated value.
Calculate displays the result; Calculate and save stores it. Supply voltage, strip type and power supply losses affect the estimate. One global profile is an approximation when using mixed strips.
These measurements switch real LEDs. Stop tests afterwards and restore the normal scene or Off. Temporary test values are distinct from the saved output configuration.

sections.title: Scenes model, selection, pool and storage
sections.body:
A scene is a slot containing name, enable state, color, brightness and startup/main/shutdown phases. Valid slots are 1 to 30; 0 means Off. Old slots 31 to 50 are handled only during migration.
The visible scene count limits the UI selection without deleting a scene or blocking its KNX number. Enabled controls normal availability. In scene pool includes an enabled scene in KNX next/previous cycling, in ascending slot order.
Each phase has an effect and relevant parameters; irrelevant fields are hidden. Startup and shutdown may use independent colors. Otherwise they use the main color.
Save scene confirms the record. Copy overwrites the selected destination; Reset restores that slot's defaults. First check whether KNX uses the destination in operation.
The browser preview helps with direction, timing and geometry. It does not replace physical LED tests, current limits, hardware profiles or wiring checks. Test a real output after editing.

sections.title: Phases, duration, step time and re-switch
sections.body:
Startup makes the scene appear; the main phase holds or animates it; shutdown ends it. No startup/shutdown effect skips that spatial phase, while separate soft-on/off ramps may still apply.
Duration is the phase length; step time is the interval between movement steps. A larger step time slows movement. Depending on the phase, duration 0 means automatic duration or an unlimited main phase. Automatic spatial duration depends on pixel space and movement.
The main phase can last up to 36 hours. The interface displays seconds while storage uses milliseconds. 1000 ms = 1 s; check the unit beside each field.
Always execute startup and Always execute shutdown determine whether those spatial phases also run during direct scene changes. Without them, a direct transition may occur.
When switching again during a transition, runtime logic accounts for the visible intermediate state. Test regular on/off and direct scene changes separately.

sections.title: Main color, phase colors and soft ramps
sections.body:
RGB white is a mixture of three channels and differs from the separate W channel of an RGBW strip. White controls appear where the output configuration supports them. Scene brightness, output limits and current limits also affect independent phase colors.
Independent startup and shutdown colors can be enabled separately. Without the checkbox they use the main color. KNX color telegrams change the main color, not these independent phase colors.
Soft on/off adds brightness ramps from 0 to 10 seconds in 0.1 second steps. These work alongside the spatial effect and do not replace its duration or direction.
Global phase color transition applies to all scenes at the start of the target phase: startup → main and main → shutdown. 0 is immediate; maximum 10000 ms; default 500 ms. It blends the base color and its associated brightness change.
During normal switch-on, runtime logic can replace a completely dark main color with a fallback color. To switch off reliably, use Off rather than an unexplained black but active scene.

sections.title: Next Scene Start Previous and Mixing Types
sections.body:
The lead time belongs to the outgoing scene. The next scene starts that much earlier than the end of its shutdown effect. 0 means sequential playback. The value cannot exceed the effective shutdown duration; the editor limits it.
If no shutdown effect runs during a scene change, this interval instead provides a smooth transition. Always execute startup/shutdown additionally determines the participating phases.
The global mixing mode combines both images: Averaged uses the channel mean; Time weighted shifts contribution from old to new; Added sums both and clamps to the channel maximum. Time weighted is the default.
Added can be brighter and reach current limits sooner. Averaging can darken individual contributions. Ramps, phase colors and spatial fill also affect the result. Check both the transition and the resulting main phase on real LEDs.

sections.title: Level of filling, segments, direction and synchronization
sections.body:
Affected LEDs can be specified as a percentage or an absolute count. Percentage adapts to output length; absolute count is limited to the available pixels. The shared fill setting applies to startup, main and shutdown phases.
Reverse direction and mirror at center apply to running-light and wave effects. Mirroring runs from center to ends; combining it with reverse runs from ends to center. Random fill has no fixed direction.
Effect segments divide the effect spatially; physical string segments divide an output into repetitions. Segment count 2 to 100 and lit portion 1 to 100 % define the geometry. The old soft segment edge has been removed.
Output start delay and string-segment start/stop delays are separate, each up to 60000 ms. 0 means simultaneous.
Start/stop synchronization matches the total duration across different strip lengths. Runtime mode uses the same step time per pixel, so shorter strips finish earlier. Use Output sequence for independently timed outputs.

sections.title: Effect families and migration of old effects
sections.body:
Static keeps the area. Running light builds pixels spatially up/down. Shaft moves a lighting range with optional rear lights. Pulsation changes brightness soft, warning blinds clearly. Segment Lamps Repeated Sections; Segment Rand + Mitte distributes it according to geometry.
Random pixel setup fills/empties in random order. Sparkling combines new light points, density and lifetime. Fireworks use their own speed/intensity. Tetrix builds falling blocks, keeps short and starts again.
The effect reference lists all catalog entries including import compatibility. Old IDs hidden in the selection are expressly marked.
Tetris and Tetris 2 were removed and imaged during import on Tetrix. Your previous fields for degradation type, Next-Preview, Pixel/Meter, distances and HSV distance are not hidden current settings.

sections.title: Output sequence: directions A/B and follow-up
sections.body:
The output sequence coordinates separate outputs, such as a staircase. Each step starts the last state or a fixed scene. It uses the existing scene engine.
A and B are independent consequences and do not have to be mirror images. KNX-DP 5 = 1 triggers A, DP 6 = 1 B; 0 doesn't do anything. The webbuttons trigger the same directions.
Per step use, output, action, scene and absolute start time from trigger. 0/0.5/1,0 seconds starts staggered; 1/1/1 simultaneously. The row sequence alone does not calculate time intervals.
Common follow-up keeps the result. Restart restarting at new trigger extends it. Runtime status calls overnomes, started and active skipped. Already active or externally operated outputs are subject to the property/acceptance logic and are not switched off unnoticed.
Chain followers are not their own follow-up steps. Before testing check activation, stored stand, scenes, blocking and brightness lock.

sections.title: Switch-off order and absolute times
sections.body:
Switch-off times count after the relevant follow-up from the start of the switch-off sequence. They are not relative pauses to the previous line.
Everybody ends together at the same time. As a turn-on sequence, the start sequence uses the reverse turn-on sequence of its reversal. User-defined assigns outputs and times freely. The last direction and its reversal are oriented towards the last effective directional course.
For predetermined sequences, the rows deliver times for the respective position; in the case of user-defined, the output and time explicitly determine the sequence. Double or invalid information is checked.
Up to 86400 seconds/24 hours with millisecond resolution are possible. Only with short test times check whether start time and switch-off time have been correctly understood. Save changes and wait for confirmed memory status.

sections.title: Keep Presence: Status, Trigger and Start Release
sections.body:
DP 7 processes presence as 1 bit with 0/1. DP 8 is optionally a byte: 0 finishes presence, report positive values presence. Activate the byte object separately; Otherwise, no unnecessary readings are required on an unconnected object.
In status mode, active presence keeps the current sequence; after the end, the presence follow-up applies. In the trigger mode, messages are processed as triggering with a temporal follow-up effect.
Presence is allowed to start a sequence that is not yet running. Start direction then selects A or B. Without a start release, presence holds an existing sequence, but does not replace a normal start trigger.
Presence follow-up and common follow-up have various tasks. To trigger A/B, set presence, stop presence and observe the switch-off sequence. Distinguishing status and actually effective holding state.
In trigger mode, each 1-telegram extends the full presence delay time; 0 is ignored. The byte object can never turn on itself. Both inputs maintain the same presence state, and the last telegram received counts.

sections.title: Brightness lock, hysteresis and overcontrol
sections.body:
DP 9 processes Lux via DPT 9.004. When the brightness lock is activated, the measured value, comparison and threshold decide on new start triggers. Above lock is the classic insulation barrier; She's going to be locked up.
Hysteresis prevents fluttering around the threshold. The test is carried out at the trigger, not as a continuous disconnection, so that the own light does not switch off itself via the sensor.
Without a valid measured value, the lock does not engage. The UI shows measured value, blocking, blocked triggers and an understandable prediction of the starting effect. Threshold/hysteresis ranges up to 100000 lux.
Automatic uses the measurement. Permanently freely ignores this lock, permanently locked blocked regardless of the measured value. Both overdrives are volatile: after restarting again automatic. “Permanent” applies until the next operation/restart, not as a stored state.

sections.title: KNX/BAOS and fixed interface
sections.body:
The current KNX interface is Scheme 11. BAOS object number, ETS group address and data point type are different things. In ETS, group addresses are connected to the intended BAOS objects.
Numbers are fixedly defined in the firmware and can no longer be renumbered freely in the WebUI. Old ETS/BAOS imports must fit the current interface. Global commands: 1 to 49, status: 50 to 99, output blocks: from 100, 200, etc.
KNX is a core function and has no more general activation hooks. Check BAOS-Bereitschaft, UART, physical connection and suitable data types before scene error search.
Control receiving objects, report status objects. Do not unconsider both directions on the same group address. For chains counts the head; Successors are not independently controllable channels.
The current object overview is included in the help. The truly assigned group addresses of the system remain significant, even if an import artifact specifies sample addresses.

sections.title: Switch-on mode, basic scene and switching releases
sections.body:
Switch-on mode determines the response to switching telegram 1: last value/scene, fixed RGBW percentages or a fixed scene.
The KNX base scene is the fallback for color/brightness telegrams allowed to switch on when there is no active or previous scene. It must exist and be enabled; it is not automatically the fixed switch-on scene.
Scene object switches on: enabled applies 1 to 30 immediately; disabled stores the selection for the next regular switch-on. Scene 0 always switches off.
Brightness object switches on: enabled allows a positive value to start an off output; disabled only remembers it for the next regular switch-on. Brightness object switches off: enabled treats 0 as Off; disabled ignores 0.
ON/OFF ramp duration is 0 to 60 seconds; 0 acts immediately. Scene phases and the shutdown effect also apply.
Absolute color/brightness values belong to the active scene. They are saved through the verified scene store after one hour without another change or before changing scenes. Normal switching telegrams do not write the complete configuration.

sections.title: Lock and forced control: Priority and release
sections.body:
Lock/force are configured per output; central blocking/forced objects are removed. Force has priority over lock, both over normal commands. Successors take over their head.
Active level selects 0 or 1 as triggering. Action when activating and deactivating are separate: maintain state, out or on. Therefore, release does not automatically restore the state before the lock.
Blocked normal commands are not collected as an unlimited queue for later. After release, the release action or current situation applies; if necessary switch again regularly.
To test send active level, try normal scene command, check status and consciously release it. In the case of inverted active levels, a supposed OFF telegram can activate the lock.

sections.title: Status broadcast, electricity, utilisation and life signs
sections.body:
Status mode can be passive, on change, periodic, or change plus interval. Available intervals are 1/5/10/30/60/300/600/1800/3600 seconds. Short intervals increase bus traffic.
Scene, brightness and color status are withheld during fades and sent as final values afterwards; switching status remains prompt. Transitions longer than 30 seconds do not suppress feedback indefinitely.
Current status uses DPT 14.019 in amperes and is an estimate after limiting. Minimum change, minimum interval and refresh control traffic; defaults are 200 mA, 10 s and 300 s.
Real-time load is rolling P95 loop duration relative to the 25 ms response budget, not an operating-system CPU measurement. Default reporting thresholds are 2 percentage points, a 5 s minimum interval and 30 s refresh.
Ready is 1 only after full initialization. Before planned maintenance, 0 is sent with priority. Default refresh is 30 s; 0 means change-only reporting. A monitor can detect a hard failure from missing heartbeat updates.
Error, overload and power limit are separate status types. Read time, current state and event message together.

sections.title: Time, network, restart and factory reset via KNX
sections.body:
DP 18 receives time and DP 19 receives date. DP 22 uses DPT 19.001 for a complete timestamp; check support in the BAOS/ETS tool. Time is used for events and secure online connections.
DP 20 controls Ethernet and DP 21 controls Wi-Fi: 0 = Off, 1 = On. Without the timer, stored states also apply after reboot. With the timer active, Ethernet starts on reboot and KNX ON restarts the access window.
DP 14 requests reboot. DP 15 requests factory reset only with exactly 0xA5 = 165; ordinary 0/1 values do not trigger it. Deliberately separate these system objects from lighting commands.
Reboot loads saved settings. Factory reset erases setup and returns to the wizard. Save an external backup first if settings must be retained.

sections.title: Fullbackup, Scene Export and Import
sections.body:
A full backup contains saved device settings including outputs, network, power, KNX behavior and scenes. Downloading it does not change lighting settings.
Normal exports contain neither plaintext passwords nor password-derived values. Normal import does not silently adopt another device's credentials; local Wi-Fi/AP passwords remain protected. A backup is therefore not a complete copy of all secrets.
Import checks syntax, schema, ranges and relationships. An error prevents partial application. Wait for confirmed storage and any required restart.
Scene export is separate: it contains the complete bank from 1 to 30, including disabled slots, without output/network/power/access settings. Validate before importing and again after changing the file. Review the displayed change list.
Importing across hardware profiles cannot create missing radio hardware. Back up before rollback because older firmware may discard newer fields. Keep the original file unchanged on your computer.

sections.title: Rescue Copy and Confirmed Scene Bank
sections.body:
Startup fully validates the active configuration. If damaged, the previous file is checked using the same rules. A valid previous copy may supply runtime settings in RAM without silently overwriting the damaged main file.
Recovery displays the source and file states. An administrator may explicitly adopt a validated copy or import a corrected backup. If both copies are unusable, safe defaults provide diagnostic and recovery access.
The scene bank has its own confirmed state. Editor and import may be blocked when writing is locked. Follow the reported state for retry or rollback; a browser response without a confirmed commit is not proof of a saved state.
LED pending state, previous configuration file and confirmed scene bank are different mechanisms. Record the exact state, error and last action for support.

sections.title: Rolling, registration and session time
sections.body:
There are users and administrators. Disabled user login allows normal operation without registration; Admin actions remain protected. Rights are checked on the controller.
Users use/edit light functions and the released device actions. Admin protects, among other things, network, protected maintenance, KNX basic parameters, import and access data. The current surface characterizes locked actions.
Log in requires role/password, unsubscribe ends the session. Admin: 30 minutes inactivity, maximum 24 hours. User: 24 hours inactivity, maximum 7 days. Restart rejects sessions; Background queries can count as activity.
The session does not shut off the network. Network time shutdown is under Device → Network. Reload page after password change or invalid form.

sections.title: Passwords and lost access
sections.body:
Default passwords are 123456 for the user and Admin for the administrator; case matters. Set credentials in the wizard or explicitly accept the defaults. The interface identifies default passwords.
A user changes their password by supplying the previous password and entering the new one twice. An administrator can reset the user password through the designated admin action. Changing the admin password requires the requested current-password confirmation. Passwords must be nonempty and within the displayed length limit.
Passwords are stored as salted derived values and are not exposed in a normal backup. There is no hidden master password.
Network reset changes network settings, not all passwords. If administrator access is lost, the documented service-button factory reset restores access but erases setup. Configure the device again and import an appropriate backup.

sections.title: Service buttons: holding times and effects
sections.body:
During normal operation, releasing the service button selects the action by actual hold duration: less than 2 s does nothing; at least 2 but less than 5 s resets network settings; at least 5 but less than 10 s performs a factory reset; at least 10 but less than 15 s enters BOOTSEL/UF2; 15 s or longer cancels.
Network reset restores network defaults and reboots. Factory reset erases setup and returns to the wizard. BOOTSEL is the USB bootloader; the KLC web interface and normal lighting control do not run there.
LED patterns identify the hold ranges. An inclusive displayed counter can differ from actual elapsed seconds; actual hold duration is decisive.
Additional boot recovery: hold the service button for 3 seconds while powering on, then copy the matching UF2 to the USB drive. Restarting or flashing is different from reloading a web page.

sections.title: Firmwareupdate: Online, BIN and UF2
sections.body:
Check before update version, board profile and backup. Online routes use profile-fitting files and check Manifest/Integrity. Version history and installed stand are different.
Searching for updates checks the channel. Download and install only begins with the intended action. During installation, operation and normal light control are restricted; Expect confirmed progress and restart.
Webupload accepts .bin and .bin.gz, not .uf2. UF2 belongs to the USB BOOTSEL mode. The file has to fit the profile; similar file name is not sufficient.
Settings can only be obtained with compatible Flash/LittleFS layout. Another file system size or start address can make available data unattainable. Secure externally before layout change.
After restart, the page confirms the new boot condition. A short connection interruption proves no successful update yet; control installed version after that.

sections.title: Automatic search, installation and rollback
sections.body:
Automatically search and automatically install separate options. Search uses the set minutes interval, installation a separate delay. Only searches do not run any installation yet.
Automatic installation is only recorded for newer matching firmware and only starts when all LEDs are out for at least five minutes. The preliminary note can be cancelled. Network time window must be sufficient for download/maintenance.
Beta program uses the beta channel. The installation automation requires conscious confirmation. A GET-Link alone does not start installation.
The history offers matching older stands. Before rollback secure and note that older firmware may not know newer configuration fields. Only after confirmed installation/restart is the selected stand active.

sections.title: Online connection, time and certificates
sections.body:
Downloads require an outgoing route, DNS and a plausible clock for HTTPS. Local reachability does not prove these conditions.
Time may come from KNX or an authenticated administrator browser session, subject to the source's validity. If time is missing, open the page as administrator and check the reported source. Do not bypass certificate errors by disabling verification.
Diagnostics show network phase, HTTP status and the last error. A stalled download ends at its timeout; valid previous help/language data is preserved. After correcting gateway, DNS or time, retry the operation.
BOOTSEL is a USB bootloader mode, not a normal web reboot, and does not use the normal successful-reboot redirect.

sections.title: Events, continuous log and operating history
sections.body:
The event list contains errors, warnings and operating actions. The temporary RAM ring remains active. Persistent logging writes selected events to internal flash and can survive reboots.
Persistent log mode offers All events, Warnings and errors, Errors only, or Off. Less persistence reduces writes without disabling all temporary diagnostics.
Detailed origin logging records effective triggers such as KNX, WebUI and sequences. Frequent commands fill the ring and add processing work. The live last-trigger display is independent.
Reload refreshes data. Copy/text download preserves messages. Save important entries before clearing a log. Missing clock data limits readable timestamps; relative uptime remains useful.
Interpret code, time, origin, message and current readiness together. An old error does not necessarily describe the current state.

sections.title: Device diagnosis: Understanding memory and runtime
sections.body:
Device shows version/profile, network, readiness, runtime, boot number and memory; Admin supplements modules, pins, raw data and measurement series.
Heap is RAM, LittleFS is the flash file system. LED pool budget and system reserve are separate sizes. Low heap is not the same as full flash. The course shows changes over measurement points.
KNX, LED calculation, web server, network and memory share the main loop. A slow HTTP/flash process can affect reaction time, although the effect itself is quickly calculated.
P95 is a high typical duration in the window, maximum the worst observed outliers. Sum, average, last value and maximum do not confuse. Comparison only with a similar number of pixels, scene and net load.
Performance-Reset resets measured values, not the configuration. Changed diagnostic render target begins a new measurement period. Technical block names serve specific assignment.

sections.title: Intensified performance measuring blocks
sections.body:
renderer_phase2d summarizes rendering times, renderer_backend_breakdown separates hardware output, renderer_outputs compares outputs. effect_phase2e with path/pixel/alpha blocks shows details of the effects.
loop_phase2d_fine_sample disassembles selected main loop sections. diaglog_phase2c and diaglog_write_breakdown capture log/write effort; diaglog_written_codes calls written event types.
response_delivery_history views HTTP response transfer; response_delivery_route_max_cache holds Maxima per route. Slow transmission is not automatically slow effect calculation.
Sampling does not measure every run. Create a quiet initial state, reset readings, make a change and secure snapshot. Old/new measurement periods are not unrecognized.

sections.title: Support snapshot, JSON and release test
sections.body:
Support collects profile, version, hardware assignment, network, memory, update and events. Copy or support.txt save snapshot and add time/action.
JSON interfaces show status, network, outputs, performance, scenes, backend, KNX, update and logs. They are subject to the same roll rules. Pure raw data view does not change anything.
Release check and manifest/version templates are used to maintain and test publication data. A template does not release anything independently.
Check installation-related names/addresses before passing on. Normal password values are not included. Useful are version, profile, output/pixel number, scene, trigger, accurate message and behavior after restart.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.body:
Web page unreachable: check network timer, KNX interface switches, Ethernet link/Wi-Fi, IP and standby state. After timer expiry use reboot or KNX ON; incorrect addressing may require network reset.
LEDs dark: check enable state, pending/restart, pixel count, profile, supply, common ground and data direction. Then check Off scene, lock/force, permission to switch on, limits and overriding tests.
Wrong color: check RGB/RGBW, color order and white channel. Shifted image: check pixel count and chains.
No KNX response: check BAOS, schema, ETS, DPT/values, head/follower status, locks and enabled scenes.
Sequence will not start: check enabled/saved state, steps, trigger 1, brightness gate, presence and valid outputs.
Save fails: read the exact error/storage status and wait for other maintenance. Do not reboot during a confirmed write operation.
Stuttering: compare pixel warning range, complex effects/overlap, persistent logging, diagnostic requests and network load. Correlate spikes with timing measurements and events.

sections.title: Language, presentation and language packages
sections.body:
Language sets the web interface and selects the corresponding help package. Appearance selects light or dark mode. Both are independent of user/admin permissions; changing appearance does not grant system privileges.
An administrator can upload a JSON language package offline. The controller checks language ID, key contract, UTF-8, syntax, size and supported firmware range. It activates the package only after validation; errors preserve the previous valid package.
The filename alone does not determine the language. Select a compatible package and wait for confirmed activation. Embedded English is the interface fallback. Detailed help is maintained in German, English, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch and Polish.

sections.title: Search, selected hits and jump links
sections.body:
Search searches title, description, field identifier and keywords. Multiple words narrow a; Large/small writing and German rewriting procedures are unified. Network also finds associated LAN/WLAN topics. Matching text passages are marked.
Range selection limited to approximately network, KNX or scenes. Delete search resets text and range. For zero hits look shorter/general. The appropriate headings/field identifiers are displayed first.
For function, the associated side opens and as far as the field is present. Folded areas are opened and the target is marked. Rolling, hardware and selected effect continue to apply; a link cannot enforce a missing option.
Link to this topic holds the article as a target. Reading does not change settings. German aid is available locally. As an admin, you can update a compatible current file; Errors do not replace valid help.

sections.title: Setup Assistant: all steps
sections.body: Choose language and appearance, set user/admin credentials, configure output count and LED profiles, and select/test Wi-Fi or continue without it. Check for stable firmware if appropriate, then confirm completion. Cancelling is not a successful commit. Saved fields are validated; wait for confirmation of reboot and reachability.

sections.title: Confirm modified LittleFS layout
sections.body: If the flash layout is changed and no valid configuration can be loaded, the firmware will block normal write paths. Old data can still exist physically. Only when admin explicitly confirm layout change and continue with defaults; further write processes are thereby released. Check original backup or return to the appropriate layout beforehand.

sections.title: Simulate KNX reception and send real telegrams
sections.body: Simulation leads the incoming KNX value through the controller logic and can therefore influence real light or the respective system function. A TX test sends real telegrams to the bus and is an admin action. Both are not a purely decorative preview. Check object and value before triggering; do not use reset objects accidentally.

sections.title: Diagnosis-Writing Test and Measurement Target
sections.body: The diagnosis can specifically measure log/memory writing work. Such a test generates work on the controller and, if necessary, flash writing processes. Changing the Render Target starts a new measurement period. Then use comparable scene/pixel number; Performance-Reset resets measuring meters, not the device configuration.

sections.title: Tooltips, question marks and conditional controls
sections.body:
Hover over a control for its short explanation. Question marks open detailed help in another tab. Clicking a question mark does not toggle a checkbox or submit a form.
Field visibility can depend on role, board profile, LED type, selected scene or effect. Disabled controls cannot currently be operated. Hidden technical form values are not user controls.
Edits are initially form values. Save or the explicitly named action applies them; live tests and direct controls can immediately change physical LEDs. Correct the displayed cause when an error occurs.
Question-mark links also work by keyboard and on touch devices. Status fields are read-only. Collapsing a section only hides its display; it does not disable the function.

fields.label: Language
fields.short: Choose the language of the WebUI and the help.
fields.details: The help page loads the appropriate file help_de.json, help_en.json, help_fr.json, help_es.json, help_it.json, help_nl.json or help_pl.json.

fields.label: Device name
fields.short: Free name for the controller's recognition.
fields.details: The name helps in backups, support snapshots and multiple controllers in the same project.

fields.label: Hostname
fields.short: Network name of the controller.
fields.details: Use only characters that are cleanly resolved in the local network. After modification, a restart is usually useful.

fields.label: Ethernet active
fields.short: Turns on or off the W5500 Ethernet interface.
fields.details: Ethernet should remain active if no safe alternative access is set up.

fields.label: DHCP
fields.short: IP address automatically refer to the router.
fields.details: Recommended for most installations. Use static addresses only if network data are known safely.

fields.label: Static IP
fields.short: Fixed IP address for the controller.
fields.details: Only effective if DHCP is switched off. Must fit the subnetwork and must not be twice forgiven.

fields.label: Gateway
fields.short: Router address for connections to the Internet.
fields.details: Without correct gateway, online update and help download do not work.

fields.label: DNA
fields.short: Name server for Internet addresses.
fields.details: Without DNA, the controller raw.githubusercontent.com cannot dissolve.

fields.label: WLAN SSID
fields.short: Wi-Fi name for client mode.
fields.details: Only available at the W-Build. Writing must fit exactly to the Wi-Fi.

fields.label: Wi-Fi password
fields.short: Password for the WLAN client.
fields.details: Empty field means: keep stored password. The password is not exported in the default backup.

fields.label: Access Point Active
fields.short: Starts a local service access.
fields.details: The AP is practical for maintenance, but should be deliberately secured and documented.

fields.label: Outbound route
fields.short: Priority for external connections.
fields.details: Subject Online Update, Help Download and other outgoing HTTP connections. Automatic or Ethernet first is usually useful.

fields.label: Name
fields.short: Display name of the LED output.
fields.details: Talking names like ceiling, wall left or showcase facilitate diagnosis, KNX allocation and support.

fields.label: Active
fields.short: Turns on or off an LED output logically.
fields.details: Deactivated means: values remain stored, but the output is not output real and displayed as disabled in the diagnosis.

fields.label: Pixels
fields.short: Number of LEDs on the physical strand.
fields.details: The value must match the real LED number. Wrong values lead to cut-off effects, wrong current estimate or unmatching preview.

fields.label: Equal string segments
fields.short: Divides a physical strand into equally great repetitions.
fields.details: 1 means a normal strand. More segments are helpful if the same effect is to be repeated on several equally long sections.

fields.label: LED offset
fields.short: Moves the felt starting point of the exit.
fields.details: Useful for correcting impact points, center or direction of travel. The permitted range is limited so that the setting does not accidentally generate extreme shifts.

fields.label: After power loss
fields.short: Sets the behavior after restart or power failure.
fields.details: Off remains dark. Last setting restores the last known state. Fixed scene always starts the selected scene.

fields.label: Fixed scene
fields.short: Scene that is started after power interruption.
fields.details: Only relevant if after power interruption is on a fixed scene.

fields.label: Send LED data
fields.short: 1× per second, 2× per second or each image.
fields.details: Changes are always sent immediately. The repetition of unchanged frames helps against disturbed individual images. An older free transmission interval no longer controls this selection.

fields.label: LED chip
fields.short: Timing profile of the built-in LED strip.
fields.details: Must fit the strip. Wrong timing can lead to flickers, false colors or even no edition.

fields.label: LED colors
fields.short: RGB or RGBW per LED.
fields.details: RGBW sends an additional white channel. The value must fit to the real LED.

fields.label: Color order
fields.short: Correctly interchanged color channels.
fields.details: If red, green or blue are displayed incorrectly during the test, adjust the order here.

fields.label: Blink start/end
fields.short: Testes first and last LEDs of an output.
fields.details: Thus, data direction, strand end, color sequence and physical assignment can be quickly checked.

fields.label: Power group
fields.short: Adjusts the output to a power supply/power range.
fields.details: Outputs on the same power supply should use the same power group.

fields.label: Strip limit mA
fields.short: Maximum permitted current for this output.
fields.details: The power limiter uses this value for warnings and dimming. Choose value suitable for cabling and feeding.

fields.label: Max. brightness
fields.short: Limits the brightness of an output.
fields.details: 0 remains dark, 255 is full brightness. Lower values reduce all colors of this output.

fields.label: Manual tests active
fields.short: Number of currently running manual color or edge tests.
fields.details: 0 means: no output is just overdriven by a manual test. In active tests, evaluate normal scenes only after the end of the test.

fields.label: Controller limitation mA
fields.short: Total current limit for the controller.
fields.details: Should fit the safe overall performance. The value is a software limit and no electrical fuse.

fields.label: Base current mA
fields.short: Fixed, non-dimmable current component.
fields.details: Typically from measurement all LEDs. Is counted for the total limit.

fields.label: Safety %
fields.short: Safety factor for current limits.
fields.details: Reduces usable limits so that reserve for measurement accuracy, temperature and power supply aging remains.

fields.label: R/G/B/W mA per pixel
fields.short: Current model for the individual color channels.
fields.details: The more accurate these values are, the better the current estimate fits. Ideally determine via the measurement function.

fields.label: Standby mA/LED
fields.short: Quiet current per LED.
fields.details: Only use if this portion is not already contained in the base current, otherwise it is counted twice.

fields.label: Active Power Groups
fields.short: Number of power supply groups used.
fields.details: Only activate as many groups as are really needed. The assignment should represent the real power supply division so that group limits and warnings are meaningful.

fields.label: Power group limitation mA
fields.short: Electricity limit for a group.
fields.details: Must fit the fuse and the power supply of this group.

fields.label: Test output
fields.short: Output for the current profile measurement.
fields.details: Select a well-achievable output with a known LED number.

fields.label: Measurement LEDs
fields.short: Number of LEDs that are switched for the measurement.
fields.details: No longer measure LEDs than can be safely supplied by the power supply and measurement setup.

fields.label: Name
fields.short: Display name of a scene or a run.
fields.details: Speaking names facilitate KNX allocation and operation.

fields.label: Copy selected sequence to
fields.short: Duplicates a run to a destination.
fields.details: The target run is overwritten. Previously, check whether it is used productively.

fields.label: Reset sequence
fields.short: Sets the selected process to factory standard.
fields.details: Reset only the selected sequence, then perform preview and real test.

fields.label: Building rate
fields.short: UART speed to the BAOS module.
fields.details: UART parameters must fit the BAOS module. Use current diagnosis; a random change does not solve any ETS assignment.

fields.label: Send status
fields.short: Specifies when status objects are sent to the bus.
fields.details: Passive sends only manually/on request. Change sends when state changes. Time sends cyclical. Combination uses both.

fields.label: Status interval
fields.short: Time between cyclic status messages.
fields.details: Too short intervals can unnecessarily load the bus. 0 is not intended here as a normal cycle value.

fields.label: Central on/off
fields.short: Central ON/OFF controls the released outputs.
fields.details: Each output uses its configured switch-on behavior. Locking, forced control and turn-on releases also apply to central commands. Central ONE is not a solid warm white value.

fields.label: Central Scene Choice
fields.short: Starts a scene over KNX.
fields.details: The received value is imaged on the corresponding scene.

fields.label: Central brightness
fields.short: Central absolute brightness for released outputs.
fields.details: The firmware processes the central brightness object. Output-specific barriers and forced control have priority. The behavior at 0 and when switched on by brightness depends on the output settings.

fields.label: Central color R/G/B/W
fields.short: Direct colour components 0 to 255.
fields.details: For RGB outputs, white is ignored or processed appropriately, depending on the runtime logic.

fields.label: Output input/output
fields.short: Switching object for a single output.
fields.details: If only acts on the assigned output and can be overdriven by locking/force.

fields.label: Exit scene
fields.short: Scene selection for a single output.
fields.details: Useful if different outputs are to be controlled independently.

fields.label: Lock object
fields.short: Locks normal operation of an output.
fields.details: Note active level: depending on the setting blocks value 0 or value 1.

fields.label: force object
fields.short: Forces a defined action.
fields.details: Forced control overrides normal scene commands as long as it is active.

fields.label: Action at lock/force
fields.short: Determine what happens with active or inactive object.
fields.details: Typical actions are out, one or no change. Test before productive use with ETS group addresses.

fields.label: Beta versions
fields.short: Allows trials.
fields.details: Enable only consciously. Beta versions can contain new features, but also errors.

fields.label: Automatic search
fields.short: Checks on new firmware online.
fields.details: Needs functioning internet connection, DNS and matching update path.

fields.label: Automatic install
fields.short: Installs found updates without any further click.
fields.details: Practical, but risky in trials. Use very consciously for productive installations.

fields.label: Local BIN file
fields.short: Upload firmware file from your browser.
fields.details: Only use matching firmware for this profile. Before downloading backup.

fields.label: Search
fields.short: Searches titles, pages, short texts and details.
fields.details: Suitable for terms such as pixels, KNX, gateway, forced control, backup, update or manual tests. The search normalizes umlaute: outputs and outputs deliver the same results.

fields.label: Update your help
fields.short: Loads the current help file for the active language.
fields.details: This lasting LittleFS writing process requires an admin application and CSRF protection. The built-in help remains available without the Internet.

fields.label: Download backup
fields.short: Saves the current configuration as JSON.
fields.details: Before updates, KNX conversions and major tests always create a backup.

fields.label: Import backup
fields.short: Enters a saved configuration.
fields.details: The file is validated. However, check beforehand whether it fits the firmware profile and the installation.

fields.label: Delete events
fields.short: Empty the event list.
fields.details: Delete only after documentation or support snapshot, otherwise important diagnostic instructions are lost.

fields.label: Fallback-IP active
fields.short: Enables a replacement IP if the normal network configuration is not accessible.
fields.details: Helps with DHCP/IP problems. The fallback address must be accessible in the local maintenance network and must not occupy a productive address twice.

fields.label: Caseback IP
fields.short: Replacement address for emergency access.
fields.details: Only use when the address is consciously suited to the service network. After successful repair of the main configuration, check whether caseback is required further.

fields.label: Fallback Gateway
fields.short: Router address for fallback mode.
fields.details: For pure local maintenance access, gateway can be empty or unused. For online update/help it must be correct.

fields.label: Caseback Subnet
fields.short: Net mask of the fallback address.
fields.details: Must fit the fallback IP and the maintenance network.

fields.label: Caseback DNS
fields.short: Name server in caseback mode.
fields.details: Only relevant if the controller is to resolve internet names in caseback mode.

fields.label: AP-IP
fields.short: IP address of the controller access point.
fields.details: This address is used when a service device connects directly to the controller-AP.

fields.label: AP-SSID
fields.short: WLAN name of the local service access point.
fields.details: It should be unambiguous so that several controllers are not confused on site.

fields.label: AP password
fields.short: Password for the Service Access Point.
fields.details: Empty field retains the stored password. WPA2 passwords must have at least 8 characters; empty can be interpreted as an open service-AP depending on firmware.

fields.label: Select sequence
fields.short: Selects the scene/output location that is edited.
fields.details: Changes always refer to the currently selected process. Check the right place before copying or resetting.

fields.label: Time position in sequence
fields.short: Shows a certain time of the process.
fields.details: Helps to check the structure, main phase and fading in a targeted manner.

fields.label: Preview speed
fields.short: Speed of the browser preview.
fields.details: Influences only the preview in the browser, not necessarily the real LED output.

fields.label: Global running light/wave synchronization
fields.short: Determines how multiple outputs converge in time.
fields.details: Start/stop synchronizes start and end. Runtime uses the same step time per pixel, which allows short strands to be finished earlier.

fields.label: Affected LEDs
fields.short: Defines whether filling values are interpreted in percentage or absolute terms.
fields.details: Percentage adapts to different output lengths. Absolutely uses fixed LED numbers and is limited per output.

fields.label: # Pixel / Level of Fill
fields.short: Defines how many LEDs are affected by the effect.
fields.details: Depending on the pixel mode, to be understood as a percentage or absolute pixel count.

fields.label: Start/In/Out Effect
fields.short: Selects the effect for a run-off phase.
fields.details: Start is the construction, one/main phase of the lasting state, from the lead-off/degrading phase.

fields.label: Start/Main/Out-Duration
fields.short: Duration or ramp of a run-off phase in milliseconds.
fields.details: Small values act hard and fast, larger values softer. Test real output for very long LED stripes.

fields.label: Start/In/Out degree of filling
fields.short: Level of filling of a phase.
fields.details: Controls how broad or full an effect appears within the phase.

fields.label: Step time ms
fields.short: Time between movement steps.
fields.details: Smaller values run faster. Too small values can have a restless effect in long processes.

fields.label: pulse/blink period ms
fields.short: Periodic duration for pulse or flash effects.
fields.details: Defines how quickly an effect becomes brighter/darker or flashes.

fields.label: Start next scene earlier
fields.short: Before the next scene when leaving this scene.
fields.details: 0 = consecutive. Maximum as long as the effective out-effect, maximum 60 seconds. Without an out-effect, the time serves as a soft change. Global mix determines averaged, time-weighted or added.

fields.label: Start/stop offset per channel
fields.short: Timely offset between color or segment channels.
fields.details: Creates staggered movements. Very high values can make the effect difficult to predict.

fields.label: Remarkable %
fields.short: length of the tailings or tailings.
fields.details: The bright head and the soft tail together give the visible length.

fields.label: Spark speed ms
fields.short: Speed for funkel/sparkle effects.
fields.details: Smaller values generate more activity. To coordinate with life and degree of filling.

fields.label: Sparkle filling degree %
fields.short: Density of the Funkel pixels.
fields.details: High values act more dense and brighter, but can greatly change current estimation and perception.

fields.label: Funkel Lifetime ms
fields.short: How long individual funkel points remain visible.
fields.details: Short life acts hectic, long life time calmer.

fields.label: Status on/off TX
fields.short: KNX status object for switching state.
fields.details: Sends the current on/off state to the KNX bus.

fields.label: Status scene TX
fields.short: KNX status object for active scene.
fields.details: Helps visualizations to display the current scene status.

fields.label: Status Brightness TX
fields.short: KNX status object for brightness.
fields.details: Returns the current brightness value.

fields.label: Status Color R/G/B/W TX
fields.short: KNX status objects for color components.
fields.details: Reports the actually output color: the arithmetic mean of the currently visible pixels per channel, including global and output brightness. For scenes, transitions and animations, the value is a representative mean and is sent in a rate-limited manner; an output switched off reports 0. A chain head means over the entire chain. Enable only required channels.

fields.label: Status Lock/force TX
fields.short: Re-registration for blocking and forced condition.
fields.details: Useful for visualization and diagnosis when operation is blocked or oversteered.

fields.label: Status Error Code / PowerLimit
fields.short: Feedback for errors and active power limit.
fields.details: Allows KNX-side alarm or display of technical conditions.

fields.label: Support snapshot
fields.short: Collects technical data for troubleshooting.
fields.details: For support questions, first load and copy snapshot, so that version, profile, pins, network, memory and last events are visible.

fields.label: Standard of production
fields.short: Returns configuration to defaults.
fields.details: Just run consciously and download backup beforehand. Then recheck outputs, KNX and network.

fields.label: Apply the scene
fields.short: Starts a scene directly from the WebUI.
fields.details: Works immediately on the active outputs. If KNX, lock, forced control or manual test is active, the visible state may deviate.

fields.label: Direct off
fields.short: Switches the LED output directly dark.
fields.details: Useful before updates, measurements or wiring work. KNX can set a new state later.

fields.label: Brightness
fields.short: Direct brightness value for tests.
fields.details: Helps you quickly check without running editor. Power limits and output maximum brightness can continue to be limited.

fields.label: R/G/B/W
fields.short: Direct color values for red, green, blue and white.
fields.details: Well suited for color succession testing and fast visibility testing. In RGB stripes, the white channel is not present as a separate channel.

fields.label: Live Load / Standby / Sum
fields.short: Current current estimate from the LED state.
fields.details: These values are calculated, not measured. They help to detect power-limit attacks and false pixel/color values.

fields.label: Secure limitation
fields.short: Limit according to security factor.
fields.details: Useable value calculated from controller or group limit and safety percentage.

fields.label: Dimming factor
fields.short: Shows whether the power limiter is currently dimming.
fields.details: 100 per cent means no limit. Lower values show active power reduction.

fields.label: All LEDs off mA
fields.short: Measured current at dark LEDs.
fields.details: This value is assumed as a base current when the measurement profile is stored.

fields.label: Red/green/blue/white
fields.short: Measured values for individual color channels.
fields.details: After each test step, measure and enter power at the power supply. The firmware calculates mA per pixel.

fields.label: RGB white mA
fields.short: Control measurement for Rot+Grün+Blau.
fields.details: Optional plausibility check. The value should roughly match the sum of the individual channels.

fields.label: Speed
fields.short: General effect speed.
fields.details: Depending on the effect, this value is used directly or together with step time, pixel/meter or phase duration.

fields.label: During ONE / Bounce
fields.short: Option for running or mirrored elastic movement.
fields.details: Suitable for wave or running light effects that should not only start once.

fields.label: Fireworks speed / intensity
fields.short: Parameters for fireworks-like effects.
fields.details: Speed controls temporal activity, intensity the density or brightness effect.

fields.label: Tetrix speed / block width
fields.short: Parameters for the Tetrix effect.
fields.details: Block width determines the visible size, speed the movement.

fields.label: Version history
fields.short: List of installable or historical firmware stands.
fields.details: Allows update to new versions or conscious rollback. Always save backup before rollback.

fields.label: Install this version
fields.short: Installs an entry from the version history.
fields.details: Only use firmware for the matching profile. The WebUI checks profile and filenames, yet to create backup in advance.

fields.label: Restart the controller
fields.short: Restarts the controller via WebUI.
fields.details: After network or update changes useful. The WebUI cannot be reached in a short time.

fields.label: BOOTSEL / UF2 mode
fields.short: Replaces the board into the USB flash mode.
fields.details: Use only for maintenance via USB. Alternatively, hold the service button already pressed when switching on: Green first flashes quickly, from 1.5 seconds lights green and red flashes quickly; After 3 seconds, the controller changes directly into the BOOTSEL/UF2 mode. Let go 3 seconds ago continues the normal start. The WebUI is not accessible in USB flash mode until the board has been restarted or flashed.

fields.label: Back up configuration first
fields.short: Downloads a backup from firmware actions.
fields.details: Recommended before any update, rollback or local firmware upload.

fields.label: Date table
fields.short: Shows errors, warnings and runtime events.
fields.details: The latest entries help with diagnosis. In case of sporadic problems before deleting, secure as a support snapshot.

fields.label: LED-backend
fields.short: Shows whether real LED output is active.
fields.details: If the backend is not ready or only virtual, configuration values are processed, but not real output.

fields.label: LED profiles
fields.short: Number of different LED timing profiles.
fields.details: Many different profiles can make diagnosis and timing more complex. Configuring the same strips as you like.

fields.label: Memory / LittleFS
fields.short: Status of the local file system.
fields.details: LittleFS stores configuration, locally loaded help and OTA help data. Backup backup and check diagnostics for memory errors.

fields.label: Release check
fields.short: Checks profile, update paths and release data.
fields.details: Helpful in publishing so that manifest, version list, board profile and flash size fit together.

fields.label: Outputs / scene / estimated load
fields.short: Dashboard table for output status, scene and live load.
fields.details: Active outputs show real live load and scene. Disabled outputs are disabled with status, 0 mA, output disabled and 0 active LEDs displayed.

fields.label: Active outputs
fields.short: Counts active outputs in relation to the intended configuration.
fields.details: The separate tiles foreseen outputs and circuit board outputs are removed because the KLC board is the hardware maximum 5 and the relevant operating value is the active outputs.

fields.label: Channel linking (follows)
fields.short: Attachs this output as a successor to another channel; both act like a single LED bar.
fields.details: The chain head (Master) controls the complete chain: scene, KNX, maximum brightness and LED offset come from the head, effects run seamlessly over the overall length. The successor automatically accepts LED chip, LED colors and color sequence from the master and no longer reacts to KNX (no reception, no status). Own values of the successor remain: GPIO, pixel count, power group and strand limitation. String segments are incompatible with the linking. The test chain is run through for alignment.

fields.label: Turn around in the chain
fields.short: Turns around the pixel sequence of this chain link within the chain.
fields.details: Necessary when a strand is physically displaced against the direction of movement of the chain. The point jumps at the seam to the end of the limb and runs backwards. The chain head specifies the direction and is never turned.

fields.label: Traverse chain
fields.short: A point runs once through the entire pixel space of the chain.
fields.details: Each chain link gets its own color, the beginning of each link remains dimmed marked; a passage takes about 5 seconds. If the point is set to reverse at a seam, turn around at the affected link in the chain. Finish: the same button, delete tests or start a scene.

fields.label: LAN-Failover
fields.short: If cable and WLAN are in the same subnetwork, only one interface holds the LAN; the other goes to Standby.
fields.details: In a common subnetwork, answers would otherwise be partially sent via the wrong interface (follow: Timeouts). The parked interface retains its IP address, but cannot be reached by it. If the active interface expires, the parked automatically takes over within 1-2 seconds. Which interface wins, determines priority starting. In different subnetworks, both interfaces remain accessible simultaneously.

fields.label: Scene pool
fields.short: Records this sequence into the pool that the KNX object scene continues/backed through.
fields.details: The pool contains all activated sequences with set hook, rising to storage space, with circulation at the end. KNX telegram 1 = next scene, 0 = previous. Runs a scene out of the pool or is the channel, jumps further to the first and back to the last pool entry.

fields.label: Scene on/back
fields.short: 1-bit object: Telegram 1 switches to the next, 0 to the previous scene from the scene pool.
fields.details: Exists per channel (standard data points 105, 205, 305, 405, 505; Group addresses from 2/2/26 in the 30s grid) and centrally for all channels (data point 4, group address 2/2/4). The current scene state of the channel serves as a pointer; there is no separate counter. The hook determines the sequences in the pool in the sequence editor.

fields.label: User and administrator
fields.short: Rolls protect actions on the controller.
fields.details: Users use and edit the released lighting functions. Admin protects in particular network, KNX basic parameters, access data and protected maintenance. Backup download is also available in the user area. The current page features protected actions; direct URLs do not bypass the rights.

fields.title: Turn on/off user login
fields.body: Users and administrators can activate or disable the user login on the Security page. Activated: The normal operating area requires a user or admin login. Disabled (operated state): Operation is possible without registration. In both cases, the admin domain always remains protected by the admin password. The language selection of the surface is also possible without registration and works completely offline.

fields.title: Standard passwords
fields.body: From work and after a factory reset apply: user password 123456, admin password admin (refer to large/small spell). The user login is first disabled; Admin protection is always active. As long as standard passwords are active, the surface shows a clear safety warning. Please change both passwords after commissioning on the security page.

fields.title: Change password
fields.body: Passwords are changed on the Security page. The new password is requested twice (maximum 64 characters, not empty). The change in the admin password additionally requires the current admin password and then reports all admin sessions. The administrator can reset the user password without its previous password (which is clearly marked as an admin action); a registered user changes his own password with confirmation of the current password. Passwords are stored only as Salt plus PBKDF2 hash, never in plain text, and do not appear in configuration exports or in logs.

fields.title: Forgot your admin password (Recovery)
fields.body: There is no master password and no hidden unlocking path. For forgotten admin password, only the service button on the device helps: hold 2 to 5 seconds only resets the network settings; Keeping 5 to less than 10 seconds leads the complete set of works. After the factory reset, the standard accesses (user 123456, admin admin, user login disabled) apply again and the service-AP is accessible.

fields.title: Protected beta update run
fields.body: The call of /update/beta-latest via GET no longer starts installation: after the admin, only one test and confirmation page appears with the available beta stand. The actual installation takes place exclusively via an explicit POST with valid admin session, CSRF tokens and confirmation. Browser preview, link scanner or reloading of the page cannot trigger any installation.

fields.title: Upload your language package offline
fields.body: On the system side, the administrator can upload a language package (JSON, max. 256 KB) directly from the PC or smartphone - even completely without the Internet, for example in the Service-AP. The file is fully checked (UTF-8, JSON syntax, key quantity, voice identifier, firmware range, size) and only activated after successful testing atomar; the previous language remains active for each error. The file name does not matter, the chosen target language is crucial. The embedded English is always preserved as a fallback level and cannot be deleted.

fields.label: Pending: saved, not active yet
fields.short: New initial structure awaits successful restart.
fields.details: Pixel number, LED profile and chain structure require new hardware/storage mapping. The active plan runs until restarting. A successful storage alone does not yet confirm activation.

fields.label: Last Known Good
fields.short: Last completely successfully started output configuration.
fields.details: Only valid pool, PIO/DMA and all necessary outputs confirm the plan. In the case of a failed new structure, this state is once attempted; renewed failure leads to secure LED recovery.

fields.label: LED Recovery
fields.short: Safe condition after failed LED activation.
fields.details: LED output remains out, even if the last successful plan does not start. Check displayed errors and storage plan, correct structure and restart consciously. Pending is maintained for diagnosis.

fields.label: 0-Pixel test
fields.short: Refugee test without real LED output.
fields.details: 0 cannot be stored as a normal permanent pixel value. End the test restores the active state. In one pixel, the beginning and end are reliably tested for pixel 0.

fields.label: LED Memory Diagnostic
fields.short: Heap, pool, reserve and plans separately.
fields.details: 16 bytes per pixel for four pixels, 64 blackout pixels per active output and fixed test pool. LED budget 128 KiB, additional system reserve 64 KiB. Free heap does not guarantee a coherent block.

fields.label: Automatically turn off network after
fields.short: From / 1 min / 30 min / 1 h / 2 h / 6 h / 24 h.
fields.details: With active timer, LAN starts after restarting. After a period of time, LAN and Wi-Fi exit, the site is not accessible. KNX-EIN or restart starts again; Service button allows network reset. Site use does not extend the time limit. Off deactivates the time automation.

fields.label: Global phase color transition
fields.short: Soft basic color change at the beginning of the target phase.
